formation.explanation: A follower whose heartbeat timer expires while it is an eligible voter transitions to Candidate and runCandidate starts a pre-vote campaign (preElectSelf) that proposes currentTerm+1 without touching the term. Each other voter answers in requestPreVote with the leader-stickiness, membership and log-up-to-date guards and without persisting anything. If a quorum of pre-votes is granted the candidate runs electSelf, which persists the new term and a self-vote, then requests votes; voters persist the vote in requestVote subject to the same guards plus one-vote-per-term. The first tally to reach quorumSize() sets the candidate to Leader. The leader then appends a no-op for its term and replicates; the commitment struct advances commitIndex only when an actual quorum's matchIndex reaches at least startIndex, the first index of the leader's own term.

context.explanation: Authority is the durable current term plus the durable per-term vote; there is no global leader identity. setCurrentTerm persists a term before it is exposed and setState clears the known leader on every transition. A newer term seen in RequestVote or AppendEntries forces a step-down and term update, so context is lost by observation, not by a clock. Leadership transfer pre-replicates to the target and sends TimeoutNow; the target marks candidateFromLeadershipTransfer so that it skips pre-vote and is not stepped down by an equal-term AppendEntries from the outgoing leader, and the flag is cleared after the candidate run. The configuration context is the pair (latest, committed); latest is in effect from the moment its entry is appended.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet in three places. (1) Eligibility for formation is read from the configuration context: only voters of the latest configuration are asked for votes and only their match indexes count for commitment, and the commitment struct is rebuilt from the configuration at leader setup and at each configuration change. (2) The leader's advancement duty is gated by its term context: configurationChangeChIfStable is only non-nil once latest==committed and the leader has committed an entry of its own term (commitIndex >= startIndex), which is why a no-op is dispatched on election even with no client work. (3) Old work is bounded by present authority: a persisted vote is only honoured for its own term, an AppendEntries reply that reports a newer term drives handleStaleTerm and a step-down, a conflicting suffix truncation rolls latest back to committed, and on step-down the leader fails all inflight log futures with ErrLeadershipLost while replication goroutines are stopped.

open_details: appendEntries has an explicit TODO (raft.go:1541): if StoreLogs fails after a truncation, lastLog is left stale. Whether any real store can fail there, and its consequence, is unresolved.
electSelf returns a nil response channel when persisting the self-vote fails (raft.go:2023), leaving the candidate to wait out its election timer; this is a storage-failure path only.

checkLeaderLease assumes leaderState.replState contains every voter of the latest configuration (raft.go:1054); ordering on the main thread appears to guarantee this, but a nil-map lookup would panic and was not tested.

The pre-vote path treats a transport 'unexpected command' error as a granted pre-vote (raft.go:2084-2090), which is intentional for mixed versions but was not analysed for a genuinely unreachable peer.

Four implementation-level duties on the mapped paths are confirmed in scope and belong to their claim/check records rather than here: batching FSMs never receive ConfigurationStore.StoreConfiguration (claim-config-store-delivery); the heartbeat fast path reaches appendEntries without checkRPCHeader (claim-heartbeat-header-gate); TimeoutNow grants the pre-vote-skipping vote privilege without attributing the sender to the configuration (claim-timeout-now-attribution); and an accepted InstallSnapshot retains and reports an unconfirmed log tail (claim-install-snapshot-alignment). Their residual premises - real-deployment reachability, election/quorum consequence, contract exemption and tail lifetime - remain open.
The ReloadConfig notification scope (only a decreased HeartbeatTimeout signals the notify channels) and the processHeartbeat concurrency contract are recorded as leads/limits with no obligation.
core_overview.rationale: Both core relationships are explained from read code and the membership design document, and the connection (configuration context gating formation, own-term commit gating configuration changes, and stale/old work being bounded by term and vote context) is sourced. Residual anomalies are local and recorded under open_details rather than blocking the overview.

question.question: Does every client-facing future the library hands to a caller have a way to complete after the node shuts down - either because a raft loop responded it or because it carries the node's shutdown channel - or can a request that was accepted into a buffered channel be dropped by shutdown with no response and no shutdown escape, leaving the caller blocked in Error() forever?
question.importance: The library documents Future.Error as returning generic raft errors such as ErrLeadershipLost or ErrRaftShutdown, and callers are told to check it. A request that the library accepted and then dropped on shutdown leaves the caller with no error path at all: with BatchApplyCh the apply channel is buffered, so Apply can return a future for a request the loops never see, and Shutdown closes the node without draining that buffer. The consequence is a permanently blocked caller (a hang in application code, for example a goroutine holding a lock) rather than a consensus-safety violation, which is why it is classified as an implementation-semantics duty on the client contract.
contexts: BatchApplyCh enabled so the apply channel is buffered
shutdown before the loops consume the queued request
event_paths: Apply -> applyCh buffer -> Shutdown -> no loop dequeues the request -> future unresponded and with no shutdown escape
Apply -> applyCh -> leaderLoop dispatch -> commit -> processLogs responds the future

supporting_behavior_ids.b-leader-loop-commit-consume: The A1 path that normally responds an accepted operation, and the place whose deferred cleanup responds only what it has already taken on, which is why a buffered request can be left out.
supporting_behavior_ids.b-commit-index-advance: Supplies the advancement lifecycle the client's completion belongs to: the future is answered when the entry commits.

counterevidence: Shutdown is usually the end of the process, so a blocked caller may not matter; the library may consider completion guarantees unnecessary once Close has been requested.
With the default BatchApplyCh=false the apply channel is unbuffered, so a send only succeeds when a loop is receiving it, which narrows the window to the moment of shutdown.
The docs for Apply mention an enqueue timeout rather than a completion guarantee, so the duty may be weaker than the question states.
unknowns: Whether other future types (VerifyLeader's verifyFuture, configurationChangeFuture, userSnapshotFuture) have the same gap.
Whether a caller can observe the difference in a supported way rather than by inspecting the future's internals.
Whether the maintainers intend Error to be blocking-until-shutdown only for futures the library explicitly wires.
question.trigger_rationale: Reading the client facing future types after the earlier findings showed that the library wires a shutdown escape into some futures (restoreFuture in restoreUserSnapshot and installSnapshot, configurationsFuture in takeSnapshot) but not into the logFuture created by Apply, ApplyLog and Barrier, while the deferError.Error implementation returns ErrRaftShutdown only through that field. A local construction run of the buffered case observed responded_after_shutdown=false and shutdown_escape=false after Shutdown, so the gap is an observed condition rather than a guess; the next action is to fix the observation as a check.

candidates.stop_reason: Fifth candidate, grounded on the accepted map. The library wires a shutdown escape into some futures but not into the logFuture returned by Apply/ApplyLog/Barrier, and Error returns ErrRaftShutdown only through that field; with the documented BatchApplyCh option a request can be accepted into the buffer and then dropped by Shutdown, which a local construction run confirmed leaves the future with neither a response nor an escape. The claim fixes the completion duty without asserting the violation; whether other future types share the gap, whether the maintainers intend the asymmetry, and whether the default unbuffered channel makes it moot are recorded as counterevidence and unknowns. The map gains the shutdown branch on b-client-future and the Fact f-client-completion-escape; no accepted object's meaning, identity or edges change.

Read (observer.go:58-140). The observer carries no protocol responsibility: Raft only emits Observations from existing protocol paths, and the delivery policy is the caller's, since the channel and the blocking flag are injected through NewObserver and the blocking behaviour is documented on both the constructor and the emit path. Closed as externalized rather than mapped, because the library's duty ends at attempting the send and counting drops.
Config validation and reload paths (config.go:333-360) not read.

Sourced discrepancy: ConfigurationStore documents StoreConfiguration is invoked for each committed configuration entry (configuration.go:44-52), but the only call site is in applySingle (fsm.go:118), which the batching dispatch never reaches (fsm.go:127-186). Investigated as Candidate claim-config-store-delivery.

Sourced discrepancy in the appendEntries entry paths: processRPC calls checkRPCHeader before dispatching AppendEntries (raft.go:1390-1413), but the heartbeat fast path processHeartbeat calls appendEntries directly with no read of checkRPCHeader (raft.go:1415-1436), and net_transport routes any pure AppendEntries heartbeat (Term != 0, leader addr present, no entries, no prev-log fields, LeaderCommitIndex 0) to that handler (net_transport.go:660-686, 724-733). An AppendEntries whose RPCHeader.ProtocolVersion is outside the supported window that checkRPCHeader rejects on the normal path would therefore still be accepted on the fast path, where appendEntries can step the receiver down, persist a newer term, set the sender as known leader and refresh lastContact. Whether the window outside the fast path's route is reachable with a legal peer and what consequence it has is not established.

Read while looking for a new lead (api.go:713-741, config.go:267-...): ReloadConfig stores the new configuration and notifies leaderNotifyCh/followerNotifyCh only when HeartbeatTimeout decreases, so a decreased LeaderLeaseTimeout is not signalled and the leader's current lease timer keeps the old value until it fires. Whether that delay has a consequence worth investigating was not established, and the other reloadable fields are read per iteration by their loops. Low consequence; recorded rather than escalated.

Sourced asymmetry found while reading the snapshot receive path: after a successful InstallSnapshot the handler updates lastApplied and lastSnapshot and then compacts (raft.go:1928-1953), but it never calls setLastLog, and its only setLastLog callers are NewRaft, liveBootstrap, restoreUserSnapshot, dispatchLogs and appendEntries. Its compaction removes entries only up to the installed snapshot index (snapshot.go:213-259, maxLog = min(snapIdx, lastLogIdx-trailing)), so any entries the follower already holds beyond that index survive. For a follower whose log is longer than the installed snapshot (a divergent branch), getLastEntry therefore keeps returning that tail's index/term until the next matching AppendEntries truncates it, even though the FSM state and committed configuration now come from the snapshot. Whether such a longer divergent branch is reachable and whether the window has a consequence (vote comparisons use getLastEntry) is not established.

entries.purpose: Qualified support for decision formation and legal advancement: elect a leader and extend/commit the replicated log.
entries.realization_summary: A candidate runs a pre-vote campaign (preElectSelf) that does not change its term and, on winning it, a real campaign (electSelf) that increments and persists the term and asks voters for a vote. Followers decide the vote in requestVote/requestPreVote with leader-stickiness, log up-to-date and one-vote-per-term guards. The elected leader dispatches a no-op for its term, replicates to each peer (followerReplication), and advances the commit index through the commitment struct once a quorum's matchIndex reaches at least the first entry of the leader's own term.

unknowns: Behaviour of the pipeline replication fast path under partial responses was only skimmed.

Direct check 54e71939 executed its fixed bytes (execution e69bc2007c144a7fb7e950e3827d2cb4) with the declarative prerequisite accepted matched, comparison_complete and witness_complete true, and the assertion violated: the future returned for an accepted Apply reported responded_after_shutdown false and shutdown_escape false, so caller_can_complete was false, while the same call on a served node completed. remaining: Whether the other future types share the gap is now characterised from source but not executed: verifyCh is buffered with capacity 64, so VerifyLeader can accept a future that shutdown then drops, while configurationChangeCh, bootstrapCh and userSnapshotCh are unbuffered and leadershipTransferCh holds one.

The check establishes the absence of a completion path from the future's state; it does not measure a hang's duration, and the running-node window between an accepted buffered send and shutdown was replaced by skipStartup.
